# Thermal reference data (brief-em3d-72)

Externally generated references for the thermal solver series (briefs 73–81). **Nothing here was
produced by circuitRF, and nothing here may be regenerated by it.** Every number comes from a closed
form evaluated in a short Python script, a general-purpose BVP/IVP solver from SciPy, or an independent
open-source finite-element library — and each case folder says which.

The findings these references support, and the spike's answers to the brief's questions (Q1–Q8), are in
[`docs/design/em-3d-f3-spike-findings.md`](../../docs/design/em-3d-f3-spike-findings.md).

## The rules (R-em3d72-1)

- **The data is fixed.** The scripts are here so the data can be audited and regenerated **by hand**;
  no test and no CI job runs them. A gate compares circuitRF against the committed `*.csv`/`*.json`.
- **SI in every file, temperatures in °C**, each CSV column headed with its unit in brackets
  (`s [m]`, `T [degC]`, `k [W/(m K)]`). Lines starting `#` are comments.
- **Tables are interpolated piecewise-linearly in T**, clamped at the ends. Every table-driven reference
  here assumes that, so the solver must interpolate the same way to reproduce it.
- **Nothing under `src/` or `tests/` may import, copy or call anything here.** `spike/` is spike material
  in the stronger sense: throwaway harnesses whose results are recorded, not code anyone builds on.

## Cases

| Case | Folder | Method | Pins |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | [`slab/`](slab/) | closed form | Dirichlet, Neumann, volumetric source; P2 exact |
| S2 | [`composite/`](composite/) | closed form | the interface jump ΔT = q″R″ |
| S3 | [`robin/`](robin/) | closed form | convection faces |
| S4 | [`kslab/`](kslab/) | Kirchhoff closed form; BVP for a k(T) table | Newton on k(T) |
| S5 | [`spreading/`](spreading/) | layered-channel Fourier series + 3D FEM ladder | spreading resistance |
| S6 | [`fingers/`](fingers/) | 3D FEM ladder + the same series | the 8 × 8 Rth matrix |
| W1 | [`wire-rho/`](wire-rho/) | closed form + BVP check | runaway and fusing currents |
| W1b | [`wire-ends/`](wire-ends/) | closed form + BVP check | unequal ends, hot-spot position, α → 0 |
| W2 | [`wire-rho-k/`](wire-rho-k/) | shooting + BVP | ρ(T) and k(T) tables; the steady-state limit |
| W3 | [`wire-rf/`](wire-rf/) | shooting + BVP, exact Bessel R′_ac | RF heat, harmonics |
| W4 | [`wire-mould/`](wire-mould/) | closed form + BVP check | lateral loss into a mould |
| W5 | [`shah/`](shah/) | — | **not done**: waits for the paper |
| Z1 | [`zth-slab/`](zth-slab/) | closed form + finite differences | Z_th(jω) |
| Z2 | [`pulse/`](pulse/) | closed form + Fourier sums | pulsed peak; harmonic truncation |
| — | [`metals/`](metals/) | cited tables | ρ(T), k(T) of Au, Cu, Al, Ag |

## Regenerating

Everything was produced on 2026-09-28 on an Apple M4 (10 cores, 16 GB), macOS 27.0, with:

| Tool | Version | Licence | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python | 3.13.1 | PSF | |
| NumPy | 2.5.3 | BSD-3 | |
| SciPy | 1.18.1 | BSD-3 | `solve_bvp`, `solve_ivp`, Bessel functions, sparse solves |
| scikit-fem | 12.0.2 | BSD-3 | the independent FEM (S5, S6, spike Q4–Q6) |
| meshio | 5.3.5 | MIT | reads Gmsh's `.msh` |
| pyamg | 5.3.0 | MIT | CG + AMG for the FEM solves; a comparison in Q6 |
| Gmsh | 4.15.2 (Homebrew) | GPL | **called as a program** on `.geo` files; not imported, not committed |

```bash
python3 -m venv ~/opt/thermal-spike/venv
~/opt/thermal-spike/venv/bin/pip install numpy==2.5.3 scipy==1.18.1 scikit-fem==12.0.2 meshio==5.3.5 pyamg==5.3.0
cd testdata/thermal/<case> && ~/opt/thermal-spike/venv/bin/python make_<case>.py
```

Order matters once: `metals/make_metals.py` first (the wire cases read its tables), and `spreading/`
before `spike/q4-element-order`. The wire cases with tables take minutes (W2: ~5 min); everything else
takes seconds. `spreading/` and `fingers/` write their meshes to a `mesh/` folder beside the script,
which is scratch and git-ignored.

`tools/` holds the four helpers the scripts share: `common.py` (CSV/JSON writing, the metal tables),
`wire.py` (the wire closed forms and the two numerical solutions), `spreading.py` (the layered-channel
series) and `fem.py` (the scikit-fem assembly and the Gmsh call).
